name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of all 23 tutorial steps (0-22) with per-step screenshots for visual regression testing. Exercises the tutorial overlay from start through congratulations, capturing each step's UI state, highlight targets, and progress indicator. Every player-facing step is a real click gated by the tutorial's own rail (issue #479/Finding #74 follow-up), including the box-cut and haul-debris stages the file originally skipped entirely.

expect.note: #553: cash bumped from tutorial_pit's own $80,000 (Level.ts) to $202,824 -- drilling became queued, vehicle-gated work, so this file now pays for a driving_center, a driving.drill_rig course and a tier-1 drill_rig it never used to ($52,780 together), and burns 400 ticks of payroll, fuel and maintenance ($70,044) while the lone driller sinks the 16-hole pattern. The bump is exactly those two, so every cash figure from the drill wait onward is the pre-#553 schedule unchanged.

The added waitForSelector/waitForTutorialStep only run in interaction mode (command mode never starts the overlay to wait on) and gate every real click below on the rail actually being armed, mirroring tutorial-interactive.json.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #553: confirming the grid now only ORDERS the 16 holes -- drill_hole became queued, vehicle-gated work, so they are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, and the tutorial does not advance to `charge` until they have landed. The wait is the step below; the mid-pattern screenshot above is the ghosts-and-real-holes picture #553 asks for. Start corrected from the file's original 15,15 to 20,20 (Finding #74/#75 follow-up): the tutorial's drill-plan stage gates its picker to REGION.drill, the exact rectangle (20,20)-(30,30) (tutorialStages.ts). spacing and depth both corrected from the file's original 5/8 to the grid tool's real defaults 3/6 (DEFAULT_SPACING_M/DEFAULT_DEPTH_M, Drill.ts), discovered live: neither stepper (#bs-param-strip [data-field="spacing"|"depth"]) is one of this stage's own targets (tutorialStages.ts's 'drill-plan' entry lists only the toolbar, grid-tool button, and picker canvas/confirm) -- the tutorial rail's own CSS lockout makes every other control pointer-events:none while a stage is active, confirmed by two real interaction-mode failures in a row (depth stepper, then a wrong 16-hole count once depth was fixed but spacing was still assumed adjustable). A real playthrough of this tutorial stage cannot reach any grid but the raw-default one for whatever rectangle is dragged: (30-20)/3+1 = 4 holes per side = 16 total, not the file's original declared 9. Matches tutorial-interactive.json's drill-plan step, which already used the real depth default for the same reason (it did not attempt a non-default spacing at all). CI cash mismatch fix: this command was also missing `diameter:`, the established diameter-omission bug (Finding #52 class) -- command mode defaults to 0.15 while the real Drill panel always sends DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), and computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole duration by diameter/0.15, so the omitted-diameter command mode this file's cash values were derived from kept the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) longer than a real click would. Added `diameter:0.089` to match the real click; every downstream checkpoint through the blast step was re-derived from command mode with the fix applied.

#553: the driller drives the rig to all 16 ordered holes and sinks them one at a time. A lone driller with no living quarters collapses from fatigue partway through and resumes, which is why the pad is this large -- sandbox-measured. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick.

blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, Blast Report closed. deathCount raised 1 -> 2 (#558 full-disc survey claim follow-up, issue #558/PR #569): step 5's `survey seismic x:23 z:23` claims its full SURVEY_COVERAGE_RADIUS=20 disc (siteExpansion.ts's cellsInDisc), growing the site from the starting 32x32 to 48x48 before the driller is hired at step 10. Employee hire's spawn point is `minX + sizeX/2, minZ + sizeZ/2` -- on this run minX/minZ stay 0 throughout (the site only grows eastward/southward from (0,0), never crosses into negative territory), so that formula numerically equals the pre-#571 `sizeX/2` here; this scenario's deathCount:2 reproduces identically whether or not the #571 origin-offset fix is applied and is NOT evidence for that fix (verified live, both ways). The real driver is #558's site growth alone: on the grown 48x48 site the spawn point resolves to (26, 24), which lands inside this step's own 4x4/spacing-3 drill grid (x:20-29, z:20-29). Verified live by direct reproduction (both employees' positions and post-blast alive state read from a real run of this exact command sequence): Walt Dusty (surveyor) ends the survey task at (23, 23), Kurt Hardhat (driller) sits idle at the grid-centre spawn point (26, 24), and this drill plan's CATASTROPHIC-rated blast (furthest throw 27.9m) kills both via the same fragment-kinetic-energy check (Damage.ts's processEmployeeHit) -- a real, physically-grounded double death, not a miscalculation. cash is unaffected either way (lawsuits/fines from a death do not deduct immediately). The #571 origin-offset regression itself is covered separately by the unit/integration tests added in 75a06cf, which force a negative origin (x:-4, z:-4). CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70320 -> 70648 (+$328) now that the drill_plan step above carries `diameter:0.089` -- command mode's own drill_rig spent less time (and fuelCostPerTick) sinking all 16 holes once its duration matches what a real click always produced, so more cash survives to this checkpoint. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): that +$328 offset was correct relative to command mode, but the box-cut step several steps up this same file also turned out to carry a real-time-accrual error that compounds forward -- dropped the exact cash figure here too rather than chase a second moving target. Not replaced with `decreased`: as the note above already says, cash is unaffected by this step in either mode (command mode's own trace shows it completely unchanged), so there is no single mode-agnostic cash claim to make -- holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount/deathCount remain exact since they are not host-timing-sensitive.

The file's original decreased:["safety"] assertion does not survive across both modes (Finding #74/#75 follow-up, discovered live) -- not because the point is wrong, but because it is no longer independently checkable here. In command mode safety still drops exactly on this scripted tick (50 -> 45.05, matching the file's original point precisely). In interaction mode the blast step's own waitForTutorialStep (stepId: ["scores","event-fire-resolve","hire-manager"]) drives the real clock through several ticks while polling for the rail to reach hire-manager -- including the event-fire-resolve stage's own autoCommands: ["tick 3", ...] -- so the safety damage already lands during that wait, before this step ever runs, and by here it reads 35.15 with nothing left to decrease on this specific tick. Same class as the contract-deliver step below: real per-click waiting does not reproduce command mode's precise scripted tick count. cash is unaffected by either mode's path and stays checkable. CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70312 -> 70640 (+$328), the same fixed offset as the blast step above -- this tick spends $8 regardless (70648-8=70640), and the diameter fix's saving carries through unchanged since nothing between the two steps touches cash beyond that single tick's own upkeep. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact figure -- same box-cut-originated real-time-accrual error as the blast step above, which this checkpoint inherits unchanged.

contract-accept complete: Accept clicked on the first offer in the Contracts panel. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="1"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #1 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it.
